items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I've forgotten who was engaged as pianist, but Manzie Johnson was the drummer and Wellman Braud was on the bass.

ctx.x: Bechet arranged for us to get free supper which was offered to us. The salary was 25 dollars for the weekend, room and board included from Friday evening until Sunday evening. We played Saturday afternoon and night and Sunday afternoon which gave us the opportunity to be home Sunday night.

I've forgotten who was engaged as pianist, but Manzie Johnson was the drummer and Wellman Braud was on the bass. The first weekend passed without any incidents; but the second one, Bechet was not satisfied, because Manzie had met a white girl and was accompanying her around the camp. Bechet gave Manzie hell for no reason because there were plenty of mixed couples, white men with Negro women and Negro men with white girls, all over the place. But Bechet didn't want any of the musicians congregating with white…

Then he got into a big dispute with Braud because he had defended the rights of Manzie. As for Manzie he had taken the whole thing with discretion, but Bechet had really spoiled the second weekend by his stupid reaction as to what was permitted and what he didn't want the musicians to do at the camp.
